positive answer. An explicit eight-simple-pole gauge gives an h-only Heun
flux for the inherited residual J. Its rational identity and both literal
endpoints are legal in every original prime field. Consequently the previous

    Z=(L-F)_(Hmax+1)-(L-F)_1-3Y.                       (A)

## 1. Frozen question, inherited data and coefficient-certificate scope

The selected flux has the form

## 2. Exact reduction to a scalar Heun adjoint equation

Subtract the desired 2^(-r)G(r)h_(r+1) from F_(r+1)-F_r. The result is
2^(-r) times

    [a(r+1)/2-G(r)]h_(r+1)
                   +[b(r+1)/2-a(r)]h_r-b(r)h_(r-1).  (5)

Put u(r)=[a(r+1)/2-G(r)]/A_r. Substituting the free local Heun row shows
that the two remaining coefficients vanish exactly when

    b(r)=-C_r u(r),
    a(r)=B_r u(r)-C_(r+1)u(r+1)/2.                   (6)

The definition of u is then equivalent to the single rational identity

    A_r u(r)-B_(r+1)u(r+1)/2
                          +C_(r+2)u(r+2)/4=-G(r).    (7)

Indeed apply (6) at r+1 and substitute it into a(r+1)/2-G=A_r u.
Conversely (7) and (6) imply this defining relation and make both free
coefficients in (5) zero. Thus (7) is equivalent to the coefficient
certificate with the gauge restriction (4). There is no missing source,
middle forcing row or h_(r+1) term in this elimination.

Written as quadratic multipliers on u(r), u(r+1), u(r+2), the left side
of (7) is

    (2r^2+3r+1)u(r)
       +(-5r^2-25r/2-8)u(r+1)
       +(2r^2+7r+6)u(r+2).                           (8)

These signs and shifts fix the normalized equation used in the exact
finite system.

## 3. The explicit positive solution and a paper-checkable identity

The fixed G from (2) has this complete proper partial-fraction table:

    poles:       -6,       -5,      -4,       -3,    -2
    residues:    69, -2299/8,  1613/4,  -1747/8,  73/2

    poles:      -1/2,      1/2,     3/2,      5/2,   7/2
    residues:   73/2,  -1747/8,  1613/4,  -2299/8,    69.            (9)

For example the outer entries at -7 and -3/2 that might occur on
shifting the prior nu tables have zero combined coefficient. Equation(9)
follows by combining the prescribed nu_S/2 and 2nu_P entries; it does not
use any actual h values.

The solution in the frozen class is

    u(r)=(1/12)[-23/(r+4)+87/(r+3)-105/(r+2)+41/(r+1)
                   +41/(r-1/2)-105/(r-3/2)
                              +87/(r-5/2)-23/(r-7/2)].              (10)

All polynomial coefficients and all double-pole coefficients in (4) are
zero. The unused simple-pole coefficients are zero too. Thus the certificate
was found inside the class already frozen, without expanding its support

Here is a finite algebraic proof of (7). Let c_t denote the residue of u
at t, taking c_t=0 off the eight positions in (10). The possible residue
of the left side at t is

    A_t c_t-B_(t+1)c_(t+1)/2+C_(t+2)c_(t+2)/4.        (11)

Its integer pole positions are contained in -6,...,-1 and its half-integer
positions in -3/2,-1/2,...,7/2. Substituting the eight displayed residues
in (11) gives, at exactly the ten positions of (9), the negatives of the
ten entries in (9). The two remaining possible outer residues vanish:
at -1 use A_(-1)=0, and at -3/2 use C_(1/2)=0. No pole order exceeds
one because u has only simple poles and the multipliers are polynomials.

## 4. Finite-field existence and actual-window regularity

The identities above are over Z[1/6](r): all scalar denominators in the
partial-fraction certificate have prime factors only two and three.
Accordingly (7), (6), and the flux identity obtained from them reduce to
every original prime field. Formal poles that coincide after reduction
are added linearly. A characteristic-zero rank calculation is not being
used as a proof of finite-field existence.

Legality at the actual finite endpoints is separate and essential. The
eight poles of u have ordinary integer representatives

    integer group: p-4,...,p-1,
    half group:    N+1,...,N+4.                       (13)

They are all below p when N>=6. We use u only at the literal integer
arguments from 1 through Hmax+2. Since

    Hmax+2<= (N+1)/2 < N+1,
    Hmax+2<= (N+1)/2 < 2N-3=p-4                     (14)

includes the smallest allowed N; it does not assume the two pole groups
are disjoint. Thus u(r) and u(r+1) in (6) are regular at all required
r=1,...,Hmax+1. Multiplication by B_r and C_r cannot add poles, so both
a and b are regular on that whole range, including both literal endpoints.

The row division in Section2 is legal for every summed actual r because
the two positive factors r+1 and 2r+1 of A_r are below p. In particular
Hmax+1<N. No resonant row or field-scalar replacement of an exponent
occurs. The proof never divides by s; the same flux works when s=0.

It follows that this positive certificate has no excluded prime in the
original family. This existence statement is deliberately separated from
any uniqueness statement over finite fields.

The origin endpoint is explicit. Equation(10) gives

## 2. Exact reduction to a scalar Heun adjoint equation

Subtract the desired 2^(-r)G(r)h_(r+1) from F_(r+1)-F_r. The result is
2^(-r) times

    [a(r+1)/2-G(r)]h_(r+1)
                   +[b(r+1)/2-a(r)]h_r-b(r)h_(r-1).  (5)

that the two remaining coefficients vanish exactly when

    b(r)=-C_r u(r),
    a(r)=B_r u(r)-C_(r+1)u(r+1)/2.                   (6)

The definition of u is then equivalent to the single rational identity

    A_r u(r)-B_(r+1)u(r+1)/2
                          +C_(r+2)u(r+2)/4=-G(r).    (7)

certificate with the gauge restriction (4). There is no missing source,

       +(2r^2+7r+6)u(r+2).                           (8)
